title: Safeguarded call patterns and progressive JSON emission PRD
creator: Maya Singh
description: PRD for a progressive JSON emission protocol and safeguarded tool/function call patterns. Goal: enable streaming structured outputs with resumability, deterministic checkpointing, and robust tool invocation semantics so production apps can handle partial results, resume after interruptions, and reason about idempotency and failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format: every stream must optionally include a top-level envelope that contains a stable schema version and a monotonically increasing fragment_id. Example envelope: '{"schema_v":"2.0","fragment_id":"0001","payload":{...}}'

Checkpoint tokens: runtime emits explicit checkpoint token frames with 'resume_token' on well-formed boundaries. Resume tokens must be cryptographically opaque string <= 256 chars and include server-side sequence position for verification.

Partial-object safety: receivers must be able to accept and apply partial JSON objects; every emitted fragment must include a 'commit' boolean flag to indicate object completeness. Acceptance requires documented merge semantics for 'partial' vs 'final' fragments.

Tool-call handshake: tool invocations must include a three-way handshake: (1) model emits intent with tool_id and idempotency_key, (2) platform responds with accept/queue/reject and an expected timeout, (3) model receives confirmation and may either stream subsequent results or re-emit on retry. Tests must exercise all three transitions.

Idempotency guarantees: tools invoked with the same idempotency_key must not perform side-effecting operations more than once. Acceptance requires a simulator validating idempotency across retries and duplicate deliveries.

Failure classification: streams must annotate terminal frames with an error_class field from the allowed set {recoverable, non_recoverable, partial_repairable, timeout}. Acceptance requires examples and mapping guidance for each class.

Backpressure behavior: client-initiated streaming must support a simple flow-control header 'max_inflight_fragments'. If server cannot keep up, it must emit a 'throttle' advisory frame with suggested retry-after seconds. Acceptance includes benchmark proving throttled clients do not lose committed fragments.

Graceful degradation: when primary tool pool is unavailable, platform must support automatic fallback to a read-only tool-simulator that returns cached or synthetic results and mark frames with 'fallback_source'. Acceptance requires a failover test demonstrating <5s switchover and clear telemetry.

Schema negotiation: producers may include 'schema_hint' frames early in the stream; consumers must validate incoming frames against the last-accepted schema version and emit a 'schema_mismatch' advisory frame that triggers soft-fallback rules. Acceptance includes mismatch test vectors and expected consumer behaviors.

Observability: every stream must emit at least these telemetry points as structured logs: stream_start, fragment_commit(fragment_id), checkpoint_emitted(resume_token), tool_handshake(accepted/rejected), stream_end(status). Acceptance requires dashboards to show these events for a synthetic workload within 1 hour of implementation.

Security: resume tokens and idempotency keys must be treatable as secrets; platform must never log raw resume_token in plaintext to long-term logging. Acceptance requires automated log-scrubbing test and a review sign-off by security.

Compatibility: new streaming envelope must be backward-compatible with existing non-enveloped streams; runtime will accept both and map non-enveloped streams to envelope_v1 semantics. Acceptance includes compatibility check against 10 production prompts.

Tests and QA: provide a canonical test suite of at least 12 unit/integration scenarios (partial emit + resume, duplicate fragment, schema drift, tool timeout, backpressure, fallback) with deterministic pass/fail criteria. Acceptance requires CI gating on these tests.

Documentation: public API docs and quickstart examples showing client resume sequence and tool-handshake flow must be published in docs.redwood.ai before release. Acceptance requires documentation PR merged and linked in this ticket.

Rollout gating: feature flagged default-off for hosted tenants with staged ramp to 25%/50%/100% traffic after 2-day health window and automated rollback trigger on error_rate > 0.5%. Acceptance requires a rollout plan and one dry-run in staging.
non_goals: Provide a complete language-level SDK for all client languages (we will ship examples for JS/Python only).
Resolve every possible schema evolution strategy; we will support versioned envelopes and hints, not full schema conversion tooling.
Guarantee cross-region resume tokens will survive full datacenter failover without coordination; we will provide best-effort resume and clear customer guidance.
design_considerations: Trade-off between small fragment sizes (lower memory per fragment) and higher overhead from metadata. Default fragment target will be 2-4 KB of payload per commit.
We prefer server-generated resume tokens (opaque) to avoid client leakage and to allow server-side validation and pruning of stale tokens.

Backpressure semantics will be advisory-only for HTTP/1 clients; true flow control available for HTTP/2 / WebSocket streams. Documentation will call out the degraded guarantees on HTTP/1 polling clients.
Fallback behavior prioritizes availability over freshness: cached/simulated tool responses will be clearly labeled and scored for confidence.
implementation_notes: API change: POST /v2/streams?envelope=true optional query parameter. Response headers include Content-Type: application/x-ndjson+envelope and initial 'resume_token' if checkpointing requested.
Runtime work: ENG to add 'fragment_id' tracking in the kernel and an idempotency map for tool invocations. Estimated ENG tasks: ENG-2748 (fragment router), ENG-2891 (tool idempotency store).
DB: resume tokens stored in KV with TTL default 48 hours; configuration via tenant settings. Ensure encryption-at-rest and access auditing.
Telemetry: add structured events to existing ingest pipeline under 'streaming.emit' namespace; include sample protobuf schema in PR.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope parsing/mismatch handling (10 cases).
Integration test: simulated network cut after fragment N, resume flow must successfully rehydrate to fragment N+1 with no duplication.
Chaos test: randomized drop of handshake ACKs; ensure model and platform can reconcile within idempotency window.
Performance test: run high-throughput synthetic streams for 30 minutes with target 2000 fragments/s across 10 tenants and validate backpressure metrics and latency SLOs.
Security test: verify resume tokens are obfuscated in logs and cannot be used after invalidation.
